hints.title: 2D Monotonic Quadrant Obstacle
hints.text: Rows and columns are independently sorted, but the overall matrix is not a single contiguous 1D range. Starting at which corner provides mutually exclusive elimination directions?

hints.title: Corner Saddleback Invariant
hints.text: Starting from top-right (or bottom-left), moving down strictly increases values, while moving left strictly decreases values.

hints.title: Saddleback Elimination Procedure
hints.text: Initialize row = 0 and col = cols - 1. While row < rows and col >= 0: if matrix[row][col] == target, return True. If matrix[row][col] > target, decrement col (eliminate column); otherwise increment row (eliminate row). If boundaries are exceeded, return False.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Saddleback elimination traversing from top-right to bottom-left pruning one row or column per comparison in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Brute force examination takes O(M * N) which wastes the two-dimensional monotonicity.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explaining why top-left and bottom-right corners cannot be used as starting points because both adjacent directions change values in the same direction.
